title: Demonstration seating of a six-party Assembly
summary: A hypothetical six-party composition used to test the seating diagram, bloc register and roll calls.
body: This bulletin accompanies the [[DEMO-EL-T1|demonstration founding assignment]]: 600 seats among six parties and thirteen blocs, none larger than sixty seats.
The figures are invented for testing. The canonical composition of the Assembly has not been published.

title: Division results: first release size and channel division
summary: The Assembly fixed the release at 12% and adopted Split A (35 / 30 / 5 / 30). Split B was not carried.
body: The voting window closed at 18:00 UTC. Roll calls are now published.
[[DEMO-D-T1-001]]: release size of twelve per cent — carried, 324 to 222, with 54 seats abstaining.
[[DEMO-D-T1-002]]: Split A (Endowment 35, Assembly 30, Deferral 5, Reserve 30) — carried, 408 to 192.
[[DEMO-D-T1-003]]: Split B (Endowment 50, Assembly 30, Deferral 0, Reserve 20) — not carried, 234 to 336, with 30 abstaining.
As only one split passed, Split A takes effect. The Council of Treaty Parties now has 48 hours to delay or exercise a protected veto.

title: Council of Treaty Parties delays the Near-System Survey and Preservation Act
summary: Four seats — the United States, China, the frontier AI laboratories and the other middle powers — delayed the Act and sought an Arbiter classification.
body: Four seats of the [[INST-COUNCIL|Council of Treaty Parties]] exercised the suspensive delay on [[DEMO-B-T1-004]].

The delaying seats stated that preservation zones near candidate systems could restrict missions already en route, and asked the Arbiter whether the Act falls within protected matter (1). A delay may be overridden by two-thirds of the Assembly in Week 4.

title: Arbiter: survey act is not a protected matter
summary: The Arbiter classified the Near-System Survey and Preservation Act outside the protected-veto list. The Council's action stands as a suspensive delay only.
body: The Act's preservation zones bind only claims released under the Act, and provision 4 expressly preserves antecedent holdings. The Act therefore does not seize or restrict an established holding, and no entrenched veto applies.
The ruling may be appealed to the [[INST-TRIBUNAL|Charter Review Tribunal]]. The full holding is recorded on [[DEMO-B-T1-004|the bill record]].

title: Override carried; release ledger updated
summary: The Assembly overrode the Council delay by 456 to 144. The First Term release and its allocations are entered in the ledger.
body: [[DEMO-D-T1-006]]: override of the Council delay on [[DEMO-B-T1-004]] — carried, 456 to 144, against a two-thirds requirement of 400.
The [[DEMO-REL-T1|First Term release]] of 12.0000 units is entered in the ledger with its four-channel division. 2.8000 units of the Assembly channel remain unallocated.

title: Commission on Long-Term Inquiry sets first inquiry priorities
summary: The Commission named digital political identity and the continuity of copies as the first priorities of the publicly funded research programme.
body: The [[INST-INQUIRY|Commission on Long-Term Inquiry]] set three priorities for the publicly funded research programme: digital political identity; continuity of identity across copies and emulations; and methods for representing people not yet born without claiming to read their values.
Findings will appear in the next public world-state update. Research findings are evidence, not legislation.

title: Survey consortium chartered; first instrument contracts let
summary: The consortium created by the Near-System Survey and Preservation Act has been chartered and has contracted its first observatory instruments.
body: The allocation under [[DEMO-B-T1-004]] advanced from *allocated* to *committed* in the ledger.
No survey mission has yet reached a target system. Near-star arrival times are measured in decades.

title: Voting open: Register of Antecedent Probe Holdings Act
summary: The division on the Register of Antecedent Probe Holdings Act is open. The tally is sealed until the window closes.
body: The division [[DEMO-D-T1-008]] opened at 18:00 UTC and closes 72 hours later. Running totals are sealed from all parties, including the Speaker and Bureau.
The complete roll call will be published when the window closes.
